headline: Apple's German ATT deal lets apps re-ask users who already said no
summary: Under commitments made binding by Germany's Bundeskartellamt, Apple will redesign the App Tracking Transparency prompt for German users: it drops the word 'track', matches Apple's own Personalized Ads prompt, and lets apps ask again users who already declined, plus once a year after any answer. Changes are due within about four months and the commitments run for seven years.
why_it_matters: This is the first regulator-forced change to ATT and could raise iOS opt-in rates and IDFA availability in a major EU market, giving other regulators a model to follow.

headline: Adobe Powers a New Era of Creativity, Bringing Agents and Tools to Creatives Wherever and However They Create
summary: At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed local MCP integrations that let outside agents such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini edit native Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and After Effects files. It also added CX Enterprise Coworker to GenStudio to coordinate Adobe and third-party agents over MCP and agent-to-agent frameworks for campaign planning, creation and activation, along with always-on Firefly agents and Brand Intelligence for on-brand resizing.
why_it_matters: Adobe is making MCP the integration layer for creative and content production, so AI ad-production pipelines can be built around its file formats, which puts it in direct competition with agent orchestration from Salesforce and the agencies.

headline: OpenAI's new business agents give brands a free way into the conversation it's also selling as an ad
summary: OpenAI launched Business Hub in beta, where brands claim and verify ChatGPT profiles, plus free US business agents built from a brand's product feed. These are the organic version of the sponsored agent ad format it began testing in September. Brands get an insights dashboard but no conversation transcripts.
why_it_matters: OpenAI now controls both organic and paid brand presence in ChatGPT, which pressures GEO vendors and limits the data brands get back.

headline: Basis Expands AI Capabilities to Power Intelligence, Automation and Governance Across Advertising
summary: Basis released an MCP server that gives agents built in Claude, ChatGPT or custom tools read and write access to strategy, planning, campaign intelligence, activation and operations. It also added Morning Consult research to its Compass AI and launched an agentic Audience Marketplace with Dstillery's DS-1 as the first partner.
why_it_matters: A full-stack buying platform giving outside agents write access to activation, and buying audiences agent-to-agent, makes MCP a real buying channel rather than just a demo.

headline: OpenAI increases its ChatGPT Ads presence in 44 countries through an exclusive reseller partnership with Aleph
summary: Aleph is now the exclusive ChatGPT Ads reseller in 44 markets across Latin America, Europe and Central Asia, the Middle East and Africa, and Asia-Pacific. Advertisers can sign contracts, be billed locally and get onboarding and support from Aleph teams.
why_it_matters: OpenAI is using the reseller model that Meta, Google and TikTok used to grow internationally, so ChatGPT Ads will become easier to buy outside the US.

headline: Google Ads Now Runs In AI Mode Across 10 More Countries
summary: Google expanded ads in AI Mode to 10 more English-language markets, including Australia, Canada and India, and launched multi-turn ads in the US that can appear on follow-up questions. AI Mode performance still cannot be reported separately from other campaign data.
why_it_matters: AI Mode inventory is growing worldwide while staying blended into standard reporting, so advertisers can't measure its ROAS on its own.

headline: Can web users trust ad tech's server-side shift?
summary: With Safari now blocking identity-resolution vendors, ad tech is moving ad calls to publisher-controlled servers, led by IAB Tech Lab's open-source Trusted Server. Its 'edge cookie' is partly a hash of the user's IP address and can survive cookie clearing. It has no privacy defaults, so publishers decide whether to pass it to other vendors.
why_it_matters: Server-side identity is becoming the industry's main workaround for Apple's identity block, which hands control of signals, and responsibility for compliance, to publishers.

headline: 'We are looking more now': The Trade Desk is eyeing the M&A aisle
summary: After the company's first revenue decline since its IPO, CEO Jeff Green said on the Q3 call that The Trade Desk is looking at acquisitions more than it has in the past. It has about $1.65B in cash and short-term investments and no debt. Critics point to gaps in its identity and retail transaction data, though the article does not say the company is pursuing either.
why_it_matters: If the largest independent DSP starts buying companies, identity and commerce-data vendors become likely targets as it tries to compete with Amazon.

headline: Shopify Noses Further Into Ad Tech With Campaign Autopilot Expansion
summary: Shopify is expanding Campaign Autopilot, its agentic ad product where merchants pay only per sale and Shopify carries the media risk. It runs across Meta, Microsoft Advertising, Snapchat, email and the Shop app, with X in the pipeline, and builds on Shopify's first-party commerce data.
why_it_matters: A pay-per-sale model built on one of the largest pools of first-party commerce data outside Amazon and Walmart could pull SMB budgets away from DSPs, retail media and agencies.

headline: Adobe and Google Deepen Partnership to Bring Leading AI Models and Integrated Workflows to Creatives and Enterprises
summary: At Adobe MAX, Adobe and Google announced that Google's image and video models are coming to Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere and Express, and that Adobe creative tools are coming to Gemini, Gemini Enterprise and AI Mode in Google Search. Acrobat will also be built into Google Workspace.
why_it_matters: Adobe's creative tools are becoming part of Google's AI search and agent surfaces, which affects where ad creative gets made, though the release names no Google Ads or GenStudio integration.

headline: Iterable Opens Its Platform to Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor With a Hosted MCP Server
summary: In its Winter Product Launch, Iterable added a hosted MCP server. Marketers can build and stage journeys, preview emails and check campaign performance from Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor, signing in with their own login or SSO, and requests go through its Nova Agent. Iterable also added ad audience syncs for Reddit Ads, ChatGPT Ads, Snapchat and Microsoft Advertising.
why_it_matters: Customer engagement platforms are moving from open-source MCP tools you run yourself to hosted, SSO-controlled servers, which makes them easier for large companies to adopt.

headline: LinkedIn brings its B2B ad targeting to U.K. connected TVs
summary: LinkedIn opened its CTV ads to all UK advertisers, with LG and Titan OS as supply partners, so they can target streaming viewers by job role, industry and seniority. Cisco's test reported 52% incremental reach beyond in-feed ads, while agencies criticized high pricing and minimum spends.
why_it_matters: B2B targeting based on professional identity is moving onto CTV outside North America, competing with ABM vendors and B2B data offerings in DSPs.

headline: Reddit Taps Qloo To Strengthen Its Predictive Targeting
summary: Reddit is licensing more than 10 years of Qloo's cross-category taste data to target ads, and says new campaigns can now be optimized without engagement data or personal browsing and search history. Reddit claims advertisers see results right away instead of after days or weeks of learning.
why_it_matters: A platform is using privacy-light affinity data to shorten the cold-start period for new advertisers.

headline: Agent Inbox for Meta Ads: The Ads Uploader MCP Can Now Analyze, Edit, and Launch, With Approval Wherever You Want It
summary: Ads Uploader added Agent Inbox, a review queue where AI agents using its MCP for Meta Ads propose launches and edits for a person to approve, with Off, Approval or Allowed settings per account. The MCP can now also analyze performance and edit or duplicate live campaigns. The company says agents launched 108,808 ads in October 2026, about 30% of its launches.
why_it_matters: Human approval queues are becoming the standard design for agent-driven buying on walled gardens, and the vendor's own numbers point to real adoption.

headline: Cision Introduces AI-Powered Cision Intelligence to Help Brands See More and Act with Confidence
summary: Cision launched Cision Intelligence with an MCP connection as the first way in. The first release connects users to Brandwatch Consumer Research agents for query management, quick search, insights and summaries, and alerts, with more Cision products planned.
why_it_matters: Social listening and earned-media data can now be pulled into AI chat tools, so it can feed planning and creative agents alongside paid media data.

headline: Adnami Launches MCP Server in Beta to Simplify Campaign Workflows
summary: Adnami released a beta MCP server that lets users find creatives, build campaigns, report and manage Supply Agents from ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code or Claude Code. It uses existing permissions and requires approval for sensitive actions.
why_it_matters: Specialist ad tech vendors are now shipping MCP servers too, so agent access is becoming a standard requirement rather than a big-platform feature.

headline: Custom Ad Algorithms Are Helping Schibsted Media Win Budgets Back From Meta
summary: Schibsted uses Nodals AI to build optimization models from its own logged-in and on-site behavior data. The models predict which users are likely to click and buy, and power new direct-sold native ads priced per click. The company says owning the algorithm and the data protects it from Apple's crackdown on third-party data vendors and ID graphs.
why_it_matters: Publishers with large logged-in audiences are turning their own data into performance products that compete with Meta, without relying on outside identity vendors.

headline: Zeta Global raises 2026 revenue forecast to $1.855bn after 46% Q3 jump
summary: Zeta's Q3 revenue rose 46% to $492.7M. It disclosed where the data in its identity graph of more than 535M people comes from, with LiveIntent supplying about 20-25%. It is buying Digital Audience and Senso to add data signals and says no third party will get access to its Data Cloud.
why_it_matters: Zeta is one of the few identity vendors to say how its graph is built, and it is positioning itself as unaffected by Apple's identity block while competitors are disrupted.

headline: Federal Express to Change Practices and Pay Close to $3 Million Fine Over CCPA Privacy Violations
summary: California's privacy regulator fined FedEx $2.975M. It found FedEx falsely said it did not sell or share personal data while taking part in cross-site behavioral advertising, ignored browser opt-out signals, and had cookie controls that did not work. FedEx must audit its tracking tools and test opt-out compliance every quarter.
why_it_matters: California keeps enforcing against advertisers whose pixels and tags share data for targeting while their privacy statements say otherwise.

headline: Deezer and LiveRamp partnership boosts audio addressability
summary: Deezer is adding LiveRamp's Authenticated Traffic Solution so advertisers can address and measure its audio inventory, with a framework for sharing data among Deezer, advertisers and agencies. Through Deezer for Business, it will offer LiveRamp identity to eligible B2B publisher partners.
why_it_matters: This is one of LiveRamp's first new publisher identity deals since Publicis completed its acquisition, extending authenticated identity into European streaming audio.

headline: AudienceMix Expands Data Curation Platform Through Strategic Partnership with Alliant
summary: AudienceMix added Alliant's more than 6,000 consumer audiences, including AnalyticsIQ data, to its catalog of more than 20,000 segments, which is available in DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP, Viant and StackAdapt. AI buying agents can reach the catalog through AudienceMix's MCP server.
why_it_matters: Third-party data is being packaged so AI buying agents, not just human traders, can find and buy it directly.

headline: Supermetrics AI campaign tool gains ChatGPT Ads, its 7th ad platform
summary: Supermetrics launched Campaign Manager, which lets marketers create and change campaigns from an AI chat across seven ad platforms, including the new ChatGPT Ads. Write access is switched on per ad account, with budget caps, approval settings and a single change log.
why_it_matters: Third-party data tools are adding agent-driven campaign changes across platforms on top of each platform's own MCP server, which threatens platform-native tools.

headline: Webflow launches new MCP Connector for Microsoft Copilot
summary: Webflow released a free MCP connector for Microsoft Copilot. Agents can build and publish pages and CMS content, pull performance data from Webflow Analyze and Optimize, and run SEO, AEO and accessibility checks, all logged with AI attribution.
why_it_matters: Web experience and optimization data is now reachable from Copilot as well as Claude and ChatGPT, widening where agent-driven site testing and optimization can happen.

headline: Ozone launches OzoneOS
summary: Ozone launched OzoneOS, a set of tools that uses publishers' first-party audience data to guide programmatic pricing, distribution and data enrichment, rolling out first in the UK and US. Ozone says one global publisher saw 63% more revenue per page and 3x higher prices from buyers.
why_it_matters: Publishers are selling on their own audience data as search traffic and third-party IDs decline.

headline: Criteo to Power Adore Beauty's Retail Media Offering in Australia
summary: Criteo will run onsite Sponsored Products ads for Adore Beauty in Australia and New Zealand, starting with search and category pages on web and then the app. Criteo handles integration, advertiser demand, reporting and closed-loop measurement through Commerce Yield and Commerce Max.
why_it_matters: Criteo keeps adding mid-size APAC retailers, strengthening its position as the outsourced retail media network for retailers below Amazon's tier.

headline: Prisma integration expands to delivery reporting and invoicing for the Microsoft Advertising Platform
summary: The Mediaocean Prisma integration with Microsoft Advertising now covers the full lifecycle, from insertion orders to automated delivery reporting, electronic invoicing and reconciliation inside Prisma. It is live for Prisma customers.
why_it_matters: Automating buy-to-pay in Prisma makes Microsoft search spend easier for agencies to plan and reconcile alongside other channels.

headline: Update to the Personalized Advertising Policy (November 2026)
summary: Google updated its Personalized Advertising Policy to state that advertisers may not target users based on an interest in categories that are prohibited on its ad network. The notice gives no effective date.
why_it_matters: Interest-based segments touching prohibited categories are now explicitly against policy, so advertisers' audience lists should be checked for compliance.

headline: Google Ads New Invalid Traffic (IVT) Overview Card
summary: Google Ads is rolling out an Invalid Traffic overview card worldwide. It shows estimated savings from invalid clicks filtered before billing, plus credits applied afterward, with daily and campaign-level drill-downs and downloadable reports.
why_it_matters: Showing IVT figures in the dashboard answers click-fraud criticism and sets a reference point against third-party verification vendors.

headline: New Google Ads Overview Page: Customer Journey Insights
summary: Google is piloting a Customer Journey Insights card for eligible Performance Max, Search and Shopping campaigns. It shows how users move through Unaware, Aware, Consider and Act stages and counts leading actions such as branded searches and add-to-carts.
why_it_matters: Google is supplying its own upper-funnel evidence to justify PMax spend, which may reduce reliance on third-party measurement.

headline: From AI Native Advertising to Marketing System Delivery: BlueMedia launches partnership with ChatGPT Ads
summary: BlueMedia, a BlueFocus company based in Shanghai, launched a ChatGPT Ads service that helps Chinese brands reach overseas customers, covering intent insights through campaign execution and analysis. It says first client campaigns are live with above-average performance, but gave no figures.
why_it_matters: Chinese cross-border advertisers, a major source of Meta and Google spend, now have a managed route into ChatGPT Ads.

headline: Yesterday's Marketing Technology & AI News: November 12, 2026 (Imprint raises $130M)
summary: Imprint, which builds co-branded cards and loyalty programs for brands, raised $130 million at about a $1.9 billion valuation in a round led by Khosla Ventures. It also released an MCP server that lets AI agents use members' rewards and virtual cards.
why_it_matters: Large rounds are going to loyalty and customer-data platforms that connect to AI agents, which could become a new channel for brand offers in agent-led commerce.

headline: IndiCue Brings its DSP to Cannella Media, Powering its Performance+ CPA-Based CTV Business and Direct Programming Media Buying
summary: Cineverse-owned IndiCue will provide a DSP to run Cannella Media's Performance+ pay-per-acquisition CTV business and its direct programmatic buying.
why_it_matters: Demand for outcome-priced CTV buying is growing, with smaller full-stack vendors supplying the infrastructure.

headline: Case study: How a technology brand drove a 128% search revenue lift with Experian Curated Deals
summary: Experian describes a holding-company agency running a Black Friday CTV campaign for an unnamed tech brand, using a 27M-person audience delivered through Experian's curated deals across premium streaming supply, and reports a 128% lift in search revenue.
why_it_matters: Data companies like Experian are packaging audiences into curated supply-side deals rather than licensing segments to DSPs.

headline: Databricks launches always-on Genie agents to take on Anthropic and Microsoft
summary: Databricks released MCP-based Genie plugins for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork and Grok, along with always-on Genie agents in preview. Genie keeps Unity Catalog permissions, and Unity Gateway handles tool permissions and spending caps.
why_it_matters: Governed lakehouse data, including marketing and customer data, is being made available to any agent the customer already uses, strengthening in-warehouse data collaboration.
